scope: Full exact-source and all six complete expanded types/axiom reports for precise homogeneous degrees of the previously reviewed radial finite-support reduction.
evidence_category: Lean kernel-compiled algebraic homogeneous-support statements for the explicit radial reduction polynomials; not an executable polynomial algorithm.

findings.reason: All hypotheses and conclusions use the pinned Mathlib MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous predicate, i.e. every supported monomial has the declared total exponent sum. The weight is one on each of the four input variables X0,X1,X2,r and on each of the three output spatial variables.

The product of spatial powers has degree S=sum_i d(i.castSucc). The radial square sum is homogeneous of degree 2; raising it to floor(k/2) gives degree 2*floor(k/2). Multiplication gives exactly homogeneous degree S+2*floor(k/2), where k=d(Fin.last 3). No radial exponent or spatial variable is omitted.

For d in the actual support of an m-homogeneous input P, its coefficient is nonzero. The Mathlib homogeneous coefficient-vanishing lemma therefore gives d.degree=m, and the four-coordinate finite sum splits as S+k=m.

Only even radial exponents contribute. For them 2*floor(k/2)=k, so S+2*floor(k/2)=m. Multiplying by the scalar coefficient preserves homogeneity and the finite sum is m-homogeneous. Rejected odd summands are the zero polynomial.

Every retained exponent k is odd and therefore positive. Its core degree is S+k-1=m-1. The output B is proved homogeneous of degree m-1, not m. The final expanded statement explicitly contains natural subtraction m-1.

When m=0, S+k=0 forces k=0 for every supported monomial, so all odd summands vanish and the separate theorem proves B=0. This is stronger than merely treating m-1 as truncated natural zero. Input P=0 has empty support and is covered without an extra nonzero assumption.

Only CommSemiring R is assumed. Scalar multiplication, products and sums preserve the specified homogeneous component even when coefficients cancel or the output becomes zero. There is no field, characteristic, positivity or no-zero-divisors hypothesis.

findings.check: No hidden analytic or computational premise
findings.reason: The input homogeneity is an explicit algebraic hypothesis. No output homogeneity, coefficient bound, invariant decomposition, convergence statement or computational behavior is assumed. The previously defined Even/Odd objects are used unchanged.

trust.cache_disclosure: Existing pinned library/prior-audit object cache and newly compiled continuation objects reused; this is not a source dependency rebuild.

pinned_library_reads.purpose: Actual homogeneous predicate, zero-polynomial convention, support coefficient test and sum/product/power/scalar multiplication rules.

limitations: Homogeneous degree m means support in that degree. It does not assert nonvanishing or totalDegree=m when the output is zero; zero belongs to every homogeneous component.
The odd output has homogeneous degree m-1 and is zero when m=0. Replacing this with an exact degree-m claim for B would be incorrect.
Coefficient L1 estimates, invariant spinor polynomial decomposition, analytic convergence and physical analytic-plus-distance descent remain separate obligations.
The underlying MvPolynomial definitions remain noncomputable at this level. No executable rational representation, runtime or bit-cost bound is supplied.
Existing cache-based compilation evidence is not an isolated source-dependency rebuild.
